Lean covers every clause of Prop 7.2: existence with (7.13) on H_w, tangency, (7.5) with the printed π_m, descent, supports, uniform (7.14)–(7.15) and the one-sided clause. But every route from the paper's source bound to (7.14)–(7.15) assumes a UniformWaveClass whose copyEnvelope weight vanishes off the closed rectangles, and requires smoothness on all of s.domain × Plane. That forces temporal zero extension, which the paper explicitly does not assume. The hypothesis is therefore strictly stronger, so the relation is lean_weaker and the verdict SINGLE_SOURCE_DELTA (medium). The main chain is unaffected via current_source_class. The PAIRING skeptic's ModalControl-based (7.5) and tangency declarations replace the ModalCopyControl ones. Uniqueness only for the projected ODE and bounds only on the open interval stay low.

findings.summary: ParticularCopyBounds.uniform_coefficients_jets, the general bound, assumes frame-level forcing bounds on the closed pulse interval. All six constructors of that hypothesis take a source class weighted by copyEnvelope, zero off the closed rectangles, so such a source vanishes beyond both pulse endpoints. Proposition 7.2 does not assume that.

Uniqueness is proved only among solutions of the projected ODE (7.13), with two-sided derivatives even at the endpoints. Uniqueness among pairs (t_m, π_m) with tangency, zero data and (7.5) is not stated. The converse step is routine.

On the actual chain, the derivative bounds and the joint and one-sided smoothness of t_m and π_m are proved only on the open pulse interval Ioo 0 L, or for κ-localized sums with tsupport κ ⊆ Ioo a b. The paper states the bounds on the closed interval 0≤v≤L_s.

Two encoding choices: the general bound theorem takes frame-level inputs, which scaledControl discharges, and the degrees b'_I, a'_I are merged into one degree p on S·max(1,δ⁻¹). The merge is equivalent because the paper's δ = min{1,…} ≤ 1.
Descent, joint smoothness and the one-sided τ=0 clause are stated for the κ-localized periodized sum, not for the uncut t_m and π_m.
